full_text_zh:
[P1] 宝贝，SOPHIE
SHYOSAURUS
别害羞
[英] 布莱恩·摩西◎著 [英] 迈克·戈登◎绘
王甜甜 吕海涛◎译

北方联合出版传媒(集团)股份有限公司
万卷出版公司

[P2] 你能找得到害羞的小恐龙苏菲吗？
Can you see
Sophie Shyosaurus?
苏菲真的非常非常害羞，
每当有客人来访，
她都会躲得远远的。
Sophie really is very shy and
quite often, when visitors call,
she hides away.
不过，也许你能从图片中找到她？
But maybe you can spot her?

[P3] 苏菲不喜欢见成年恐龙。她会脸红，
说话也变得结结巴巴。
Sophie doesn't like meeting adult
dinosaurs. She blushes and gets
tongue-tied.
她永远都不知道该说些什么。
She never knows what to say.

[P4] 苏菲很想参加聚会，可是她又不喜欢和
自己不认识的恐龙待在一起。
Sophie wants to go to parties, but she isn't
happy being with dinosaurs she doesn't know.
于是，她就哀求妈妈形影不离地陪着自己，
直到她找到能够一起玩的朋友。
She asks her Mum to stay with her until
she finds someone she can play with.

[P5] 在学校里，每当轮到她上台面对同学说话的时候，苏菲就会感到害羞极了。她的舌头开始打结，大脑一片空白，把该说的话忘得一干二净。
Sophie feels shy when she's asked
to talk in front of her class at school.
Her mouth goes dry and she
can't think of what to say.
有时候，她甚至会开始掉眼泪。
Sometimes she starts to cry.

[P6] 苏菲的爸爸妈妈常常告诉她不必为此而担忧。
Sophie's Mum and Dad are always
telling her not to worry about it.
“感到害羞并没有什么大不了，”她爸爸对她说。
“每个人都会时不时地感到害羞。”
“It's OK to feel shy,” her Dad
tells her. “Everyone feels shy at
some time or other.”

[P7] “当我第一次到野兽大厦里我工作的那家宾馆见经理的时候，”
苏菲的爸爸说，“我就不知道该说什么。”
“When I first met the manager at Beastly Towers,
the hotel where I work,” Sophie's Dad explained,
“I just didn't know what to say.”
“当我终于能够开口说话的时候，说的话也根本
前言不搭后语。这全都是因为我有点害羞。”
“And when I did say something, the words were
wrong. That was all because I felt a bit shy.”

[P8] “可是，我一点也不喜欢害羞的感觉，”苏菲说。
“我喜欢跳舞，但只要我知道有人在看我，
我就会觉得很难为情，然后就不得不停下来。”
“But I don't like feeling shy,” Sophie said. “I love
to dance, but if I know someone is watching,
I feel embarrassed and I have to stop.”
“我能不能不再害羞呢？”苏菲心想。
"Will I ever stop feeling shy?"
Sophie wondered.

[P9] “那就试试看我们能不能帮助你，”她爸爸说，“当你见到其他恐龙时，你不需要躲得远远的。我们可以先练习一下你见到他们之后可以说的话。”
“Let's see if we can help you,” her Dad said.
“When you meet other dinosaurs, there's no need to hide away. Let's practise what you might say.”
“嘿，我叫苏菲。你今天过得怎么样？”
“Hi, I'm Sophie. How are you today?”

[P10] 有时候，你帮别人做点什么也有助于你克服害羞情绪，
而且当你帮助他人的时候，
你还可以向他们微笑。
Sometimes it helps
to do something for
someone, and to
smile at them when
you offer.
“让我帮你提袋子吧？”
“Can I help you
carry your bags?”
而那些你帮助过的人可能就会变成你的新朋友。
That someone you help may
even become a new friend.

[P11] “让我来帮你们捡吧。”
“I'll get it.”
“谢谢！你想和我们一起玩吗？”
“Thanks! Do you want to play, too?”

[P12] 有时候，你可以带一个特别的玩具去学校，当你感到
害羞的时候，这个玩具就能派上用场。你可以紧紧地抱着它，
或许其他同学也有一个和你一样的玩具，你们可以一起玩。
Sometimes taking a special toy to
school can help when you're feeling shy.
You can cuddle your toy, or maybe someone
else will have the same toy and you
can play together.
说不定，其他恐龙很快就会想加入你们，
和你们一起玩了。
Very soon other dinosaurs
may want to play with you as well.

[P13] “每个人都各有所长，”
苏菲的妈妈说，
“你就很会跳舞。”
"Everyone has something they're
 good at," Sophie's Mum said.
"You're good at dancing."
“可是，只要其他恐龙一看你，你就会难为情，
其实他们看你完全是因为他们喜欢看你跳舞，”
她爸爸说，“也许，他们也想和你一起跳。”
“But if you feel shy when other dinosaurs are
 watching you, it's just because they like your
dancing," her Dad said.
“They might even join in too.”

[P14] 苏菲依旧有些害羞，但是她每天都在努力
让自己变得大方一点点。
Sophie is still a little bit shy, but
she's working hard every day at
leaving her shyness behind.
终于有一天，
她赢得了一枚跳舞奖牌。
And the other
day she even
won a medal
for her dancing.
full_text_en:
[P1] Baby, SOPHIE
SHYOSAURUS
Don't be shy
[UK] Brian Moses ◎ Author [UK] Mike Gordon ◎ Illustrator
Wang Tiantian, Lü Haitao ◎ Translators

Northern United Publishing Media (Group) Co., Ltd.
Wanjuan Publishing Company

[P2] Can you see the shy little dinosaur Sophie?
Can you see
Sophie Shyosaurus?
Sophie really is very shy and
quite often, when visitors call,
she hides away.
But maybe you can spot her?

[P3] Sophie doesn't like meeting adult dinosaurs. She blushes and gets tongue-tied.
She never knows what to say.

[P4] Sophie wants to go to parties, but she isn't
happy being with dinosaurs she doesn't know.
She asks her Mum to stay with her until
she finds someone she can play with.

[P5] At school, whenever it's Sophie's turn to go up and speak in front of her classmates, she feels extremely shy. Her tongue starts to tie, her mind goes blank, and she forgets everything she was supposed to say.
Sophie feels shy when she's asked
to talk in front of her class at school.
Her mouth goes dry and she
can't think of what to say.
Sometimes, she even starts to cry.
Sometimes she starts to cry.

[P6] Sophie's Mum and Dad are always telling her not to worry about it.
"It's OK to feel shy," her Dad tells her. "Everyone feels shy at some time or other."

[P7] "When I first met the manager at Beastly Towers,
the hotel where I work," Sophie's Dad explained,
"I just didn't know what to say."
"And when I did say something, the words were
wrong. That was all because I felt a bit shy."

[P8] "But I don't like feeling shy," Sophie said. "I love to dance, but if I know someone is watching, I feel embarrassed and I have to stop."
"Will I ever stop feeling shy?" Sophie wondered.

[P9] "Let's see if we can help you," her Dad said.
"When you meet other dinosaurs, there's no need to hide away. Let's practise what you might say."
"Hi, I'm Sophie. How are you today?"

[P10] Sometimes, helping someone else can help you overcome shyness,
and when you offer help, you can also smile at them.
Sometimes it helps
to do something for
someone, and to
smile at them when
you offer.
"Can I help you carry your bags?"
And those you help might even become your new friend.
That someone you help may
even become a new friend.

[P11] "Let me help you pick it up."
"I'll get it."
"Thanks! Do you want to play, too?"
"Thanks! Do you want to play, too?"

[P12] Sometimes, you can bring a special toy to school. When you feel shy, this toy can help. You can hold it tightly, or maybe another classmate has the same toy, and you can play together.
Sometimes taking a special toy to school can help when you're feeling shy. You can cuddle your toy, or maybe someone else will have the same toy and you can play together.
Maybe other dinosaurs will soon want to join you and play together too.
Very soon other dinosaurs may want to play with you as well.

[P13] "Everyone has something they're good at," Sophie's Mum said.
"You're good at dancing."
"But if you feel shy when other dinosaurs are watching you, it's just because they like your dancing," her Dad said.
"They might even join in too."

[P14] Sophie is still a little bit shy, but
she's working hard every day at
leaving her shyness behind.
And the other
day she even
won a medal
for her dancing.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《宝贝，别害羞》的封面，展示了一只黄色的小恐龙站在水坑中，身上溅起水花，表情害羞。页面上方有书名、作者、绘者和译者信息，下方为出版社信息。
[P2] 本页介绍了害羞的小恐龙苏菲，她常常在客人来访时躲起来，并邀请读者在画面中找到她。画面中有多只恐龙在树下活动，苏菲藏在树冠中。
[P3] 本页描述了害羞的小恐龙苏菲在见到成年恐龙时的反应：她会脸红、说话结巴，且不知道该说什么。画面中，苏菲躲在一只红色恐龙身后，而一只蓝色的成年恐龙正从水坑中走出。
[P4] 本页描绘了恐龙苏菲在聚会上感到害羞，她希望参加聚会但不喜欢和不认识的恐龙相处，于是请求妈妈陪伴她，直到找到可以一起玩的朋友。
[P5] 本页描述了害羞的小恐龙苏菲在学校上台发言时的紧张表现：她会结巴、大脑空白，甚至有时会哭出来。画面左侧是她在教室前紧张地站着，右侧是她因害羞而哭泣的特写。
[P6] 苏菲的爸爸妈妈安慰她，告诉她感到害羞是正常的，每个人都会时不时地感到害羞。
[P7] 苏菲的爸爸分享了自己第一次见经理时因害羞而不知所措的经历，并解释说，即使开口说话，也常常语无伦次，这都是因为害羞。
[P8] 苏菲在派对上因害羞而无法跳舞，她感到困扰并思考自己是否能不再害羞。
[P9] 苏菲的爸爸建议通过练习对话来帮助她克服害羞，苏菲在爸爸的鼓励下尝试向另一只恐龙打招呼。
[P10] 本页通过小恐龙苏菲主动提出帮别人提袋子的例子，说明帮助他人有助于克服害羞，并可能因此结交新朋友。
[P11] 小恐龙苏菲主动帮助其他恐龙捡起掉落的物品，随后被邀请一起玩滑板车，展现了通过帮助他人来克服害羞并结交朋友的过程。
[P12] 本页建议害羞的孩子可以带一个特别的玩具去学校以获得安慰，并可能因此找到玩伴；画面展示了小恐龙们在教室外玩耍，有的抱着玩具，有的在互动，暗示通过共同的玩具可以促进社交。
[P13] 苏菲的妈妈和爸爸鼓励她，指出她擅长跳舞，并解释其他恐龙观看她跳舞是因为喜欢，甚至可能想和她一起跳。
[P14] 苏菲虽然仍有些害羞，但每天都在努力克服，最终赢得了一枚跳舞奖牌，展现了她的进步和成就。
